description:
FILED s464ay (Opus, round 22 review), Pass 3 of the ignored-tests audit
(#993): the 695 blessed rows of baselines/fail-baseline.tsv clustered and read
for cause.  This is the LARGEST cluster in that baseline -- 222 rows of one
mechanism plus 7 of its error-message half -- and it had NO recorded cause at
all.  PRE-EXISTING and SILENT.

PERL'S RULE (perlop, "Bitwise String Operators"): if BOTH operands are strings
that have not been used in numeric context, `&`/`|`/`^` operate BIT-BY-BIT on
the strings.  A reference, glob, qr// or blessed object stringifies into that
path.  PCL instead numifies as soon as an operand is not a plain string.

REPRO (scratch/p43-bop-refs.pl):

    my $r = [1];
    print +($r | ("\x00" x length("$r"))), "\n";
    our $g = 1; my $glob = *g;
    print +($glob | ("\x00" x length("$glob"))), "\n";
    my $u;  { no warnings; print +($u | "abc"), "\n"; }
    my $o = bless {}, 'K';
    print +($o | ("\x00" x length("$o"))), "\n";

  perl 5.40.3:  ARRAY(0x...)   *main::g   abc   K=HASH(0x...)
  PCL:          1              0          0     2

and the AND spelling (scratch/p42/p43 row 1): `$r & ("\x00" x 40)` is 42 NUL
bytes in perl and the string "30" in PCL.

`undef | "abc"` -> 0 is the one to worry about: undef-or-string is an ordinary
shape, and 0 is a plausible answer.

WHAT IS ALREADY CORRECT (probed, same files): plain string operands are RIGHT
in every spelling -- `"abc" & "ABC"` = ABC, `"abc" | "ABC"` = abc,
`unpack("H*", "abc" ^ "ABC")` = 202020 -- and numeric operands are right
(`6 & 3` = 2, and `"6" & "3"` = 2, the numeric-looking-string case).  So the
bit-string machinery EXISTS and works; what is wrong is the mode decision for
non-plain-string operands.

WHICH ROWS IT OWNS: perl-tests/bop.t, 222 rows of the value half (e.g. row 319
`qr// | utf8`, got '4', expected the bit-string result) and 7 rows of the
error half (row 498: a bit-string op on a string with code points above 0xFF
must die "Use of strings with code points over 0xFF as arguments to bitwise or
(|) operator is not allowed"; PCL raises nothing).  That is 33% of the entire
695-row blessed baseline behind ONE mechanism.  The companion t/op/bop.t
carries the same rows inside its blessed count.

NOT #972 (completed) and not the s464aw overload work: those are about `use
overload`'s BITWISE handlers being dispatched.  This is the mode decision for
operands with NO overload at all -- a blessed object without overload must
still stringify and bit-string.  Fix the mode decision first; the overload
hook then sits in front of it.

FIX SHAPE (untried): the decision is per-OPERATION, not per-operand-type --
perl asks "has either operand been used as a number", which PCL cannot model
exactly (no per-SV NOK flag).  The practical rule that matches every probe
above: if EITHER operand is a plain number (or a string that came from a
numeric operation) do the numeric op, else stringify both and do the
bit-string op -- i.e. a ref/glob/qr/object/undef operand must go to the STRING
side, not the numeric side.  Check the `=`-forms (`&=`, `|=`, `^=`) in the
same pass; the cluster includes them.

=== DONE (s465ba, Opus, round 23) ===

RUNTIME ONLY -- one classifier, no compiler change, no generation bump, no
artifact regeneration, corpus cannot move.

THE FIX.  `p-string-bitwise-operand-p` asked `(and (stringp v) (not
(looks-like-number v)))`, i.e. it sent every NON-string state to the numeric
side.  It now delegates to ONE classifier, `%p-bitwise-operand-kind`, which
enumerates the same box states `stringify-value` and `box-nv` enumerate and
answers :NUMBER / :STRING / :REFERENCE.  An unlisted state DIES naming its
type (rule 12) -- the arm this replaced answered :NUMBER for everything it did
not recognise, i.e. turned an unknown value into 0.

THE THIRD VERDICT IS NOT DECORATION.  Unary `~` and the binary trio disagree
on exactly one state, and it is MEASURED, not deduced (scratch/p3-perl-
complement.pl, all 14 states, perl 5.40.3): `~ [1]` is the complemented
ADDRESS while `[1] | "x"` is the bit-string op, because `pp_complement` takes
its string branch only for an SV that HAS a PV and a reference has neither PV
nor number.  `~ undef` and `~ *glob` are STRING; `~ \*glob` is NUMERIC.  So
`p-bit-not` reads `:string` and the binary trio read `(not :number)`.

TWO STATES THE PROBE CORRECTED, both would have been silent regressions:
  * CL NIL is PCL's OTHER spelling of undef (`%pcl-definedp` calls NIL and
    *p-undef* alike undefined, and `my ($a,$b);` fills the boxes with NIL), so
    it is :STRING.  A first version called it PL_sv_no and answered :NUMBER --
    `my ($u1,$u2); $u1 | $u2` then printed 0 where perl prints "".  Caught by
    the probe, not by reasoning.
  * CL T IS perl's PL_sv_yes (IOK) and stays :NUMBER.  perl's FALSE never
    reaches here as NIL -- `p-bool` answers 1 / "".

THE ERROR HALF (7 rows) is the same dispatch: a bit-STRING op whose operands
hold a code point above 0xFF is FATAL in perl, with four distinct wordings
(`bitwise and (&)` / `or (|)` / `xor (^)` / `1's complement (~)`, and `~.`
says `string 1's complement (~)`).  `%p-check-bit-string-width` raises it
through `p-die`, so it is perl-shaped and trappable.  It lives INSIDE the
string path: `5 | "\x{100}"` is the numeric op and must NOT die (probed,
scratch/p5-perl-fatal-shapes.pl).

MEASURED.
  * perl-tests/bop.t 253/256 -> 480/29 (PARTIAL either way, 509 of 510 rows;
    the last row is the pre-existing `formline` child-program drop, unchanged).
  * FULL SWEEP: bop.t is the ONLY mover in 108 files (per-file _status.tsv
    diffed against a 1fed80b worktree's run).  TOTAL passing 18266 -> 18493
    (+227 = bop.t's 227 exactly).  GATE clean, 0 new / 0 fixed, drops 5 =
    census.
  * GATE: 193 files / 6557 tests, only the 13 pclxs xs rows failing (the
    s464 state).  With the new guard file: 194 / 6631.
  * baselines edited ROW BY ROW: 224 rows left fail-baseline.tsv by EDIT
    (708 -> 484 lines; every non-bop.t line verified byte-identical and in
    order), pass-baseline.tsv's bop.t row 253/256 -> 480/29 with its cause.

GUARD: Pl/t/bitwise-string-01.t, 74 rows in 1.5 s (37 assertions x both
emission paths, two SBCL launches).  Every expectation is the OUTPUT OF THE
SAME PROGRAM under perl 5.40.3, not a hand-derivation.  INVERSE-VERIFIED on a
1fed80b worktree: 54 of the 74 FAIL there.

WHAT WAS DELIBERATELY NOT DONE -> task #1040: a numeric-LOOKING string still
takes the numeric side (`"12" & "10"` is "10" in perl, "8" here), because
`looks-like-number` is PCL's stand-in for perl's per-SV NIOK flag and removing
it requires `use feature 'bitwise'` to exist first (11 bop.t rows pass today
BY ACCIDENT of that heuristic).  #1040 carries the measurement, the
`p-box-nv-ok` arm that would answer the `$!`-dualvar case exactly, and the
one consequence of this fix: under `use feature 'bitwise'`, `"\x{100}" |
"\xFF"` now DIES here where perl runs the numeric op (it was silently wrong
before).

ALSO FILED: #1041 -- `tools/sweep-diff.pl` keys a row on file+DESCRIPTION, so
bop.t's 14 unnamed failing rows collapse onto ONE baseline entry and 13 of
them are ungated.  Found while attributing this change's movers; verified
byte-identical between 1fed80b and this tree, so not a mover.

PROBES (worktree scratch/): p1-perl-rule.pl (20 shapes), p2-perl-more.pl (the
unary family, the compound forms, the CL-boolean shapes, the fatal),
p3-perl-complement.pl (all 14 states under `~`), p4-perl-fatal-names.pl,
p5-perl-fatal-shapes.pl, guard-prog.pl (the guard file's oracle run).
subject: SILENT WRONG (229 blessed bop.t rows, the single largest cluster in fail-baseline.tsv): `&` `|` `^` pick the NUMERIC op whenever an operand is a ref/glob/qr/object/undef, where perl STRINGIFIES it and does the BIT-STRING op -- `undef | "abc"` is "abc" in perl and 0 in PCL
